text:
Sam: Quick thread — ran mbsize sweep last night (streaming chat vs non-streaming completions). TL;DR: streaming p99 jumped from ~240ms -> ~620ms at mbsize=8 on our standard pool; completions stayed ~flat. Saw kernel fallback triggered around tail windows.

Maya: Can you drop the perf traces / flamegraphs? link to the dashboard would help. cc @Jon for kernel-selector logs. :eyes:

Sam: uploaded a short trace (perf link) but pasted the key snippet below: 
```
[2026-03-17T23:14:02Z] batch_size=3 -> selected_kernel=fast-attn
[2026-03-17T23:14:02Z] batch_size=1 -> fallback_kernel=generic-matmul (cold)
[2026-03-17T23:14:03Z] kv-cache-miss on client handshake, extra init work ~4ms
```

Jon: Looking at the traces, this is classic handshake-heavy streaming workload. Lots of short-lived requests -> tiny effective batch sizes and frequent kernel switches. The fallback kernel incurs extra setup and increases tail. Hypothesis: KV cache eviction + handshake warmup amplifies the effect.

Li: Suggest adding a small hysteresis window in kernel selection: require avg_batch_size > N for T seconds before switching to the "fast" kernel, and only fall back after sustained drop. Also experiment with lightweight KV-prefetch during handshake to reduce init latency.

Maya: Do we have p95/p99 by route? Sam: pasted numbers: 
- streaming-chat (mbsize=8): p50=48ms, p95=210ms, p99=620ms
- streaming-chat (mbsize=4): p50=55ms, p95=180ms, p99=300ms
- completions (mbsize=8): p50=60ms, p95=140ms, p99=180ms
So completions tolerant, streaming tail sensitive.

deploy-bot: perf-canary/streaming-mb-sweep deployed to canary cluster (canary-13) at 3189991450.

Sam: Initial takeaway: for streaming chat, smaller mbsize (4) reduces p99 dramatically at cost of modest throughput loss; for non-streaming completions we can keep larger mbsize for throughput. We need runtime routing to pick per-request mbsize policy based on streaming vs batch and add kernel hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.

Jon: Proposed quick config change (pseudo): 
```yaml
kernel_hysteresis:
  min_batch_for_fast: 6
  stable_window_s: 8
  fall_back_threshold: 3
routing:
  streaming:
    target_mbsize: 4
  completions:
    target_mbsize: 12
```

Li: I can prototype kv-prefetch: on handshake, issue a non-blocking KV touch for most-likely prefixes. That should amortize the cache fill without blocking tokens. Will try tomorrow morning.

Maya: How big is the throughput hit if we route streaming->mbsize=4 and completions->12? Sam: short numbers from the sweep: throughput (tokens/s) dropped ~7% on streaming-heavy mixes but overall cost/tok improved due to fewer tail retries. Worth it for customer-facing low-latency SLOs.

Jon: Also add a tracing tag when kernel fallback occurs so we can correlate with kv-eviction events and client handshake flags.

Sam: Action items: 1) Add kernel-hysteresis flag + tracing (Jon) 2) Prototype kv-prefetch on handshake (Li) 3) Add routing rule to prefer lower mbsize for streaming and higher for completions in canary (Maya/Sam) 4) Run another sweep with canary next window and capture p95/p99 deltas. I'll open a short RFC and a tracking ticket. :white_check_mark:

Maya: SGTM. Ping if you need infra for longer traces.

Li: I'll post results in this thread once proto is up.

Sam: Thanks all — scheduling canary tonight at 02:00 UTC. :rocket:
